Codex Data is designed for this larger job.

Under the Hood / implementation + sources
Architecture detail · interpretations identified in context

The plugin combines analytical instructions with an artifact platform. The host performs source execution. Data’s report and dashboard contracts preserve reviewed evidence, common presentation behavior, and delivery state. The simple loop is a teaching contrast, not a claim about another product.

02 / The mental model

Agent → Skills
→ Evidence → Artifact

The agent does the work. Data gives that work responsibilities, evidence boundaries, and a durable form.

→→→
1User request
2Codex / ChatGPT host
3Skills + shared policies
4Authorized source tools / analysis
5Reviewed snapshot
6Authored React / CSS
7Verified build + shared runtime
8Report / dashboard → export / Site

Notebook and document workflows branch to their own artifact tools; they do not all run through the React app.

The host supplies execution. Data supplies the analytical workflow and artifact contract.

04 / A semantic division of labor

Skills are responsibilities.
Tools are capabilities.

“Define success,” “diagnose a movement,” and “check the conclusion” are different jobs—even if each can use SQL.

Under the Hood / implementation + sources
Architecture detail · interpretations identified in context

The 20 installed entry points form a procedural instruction graph. This explorer summarizes the skill contracts. “Common companions” means context-dependent workflow relationships, not guaranteed automatic calls. Shared policies own source authority and dependency handling; the index retains final-output ownership.

05 / More than rows

Preserve the basis
of the answer.

Raw data tells you what a field contains. Reviewed evidence also tells you what it means, where it came from, and what limits apply.

→→
Illustrative teaching fixture
18.4%

184 engaged / 1,000 eligible

This demonstrates the contract. It is not advisor research.

Provenance travels with the result, rather than depending on the conversation.

Under the Hood / implementation + sources
Architecture detail · interpretations identified in context

Real query data lives under stable keys in src/data.json. SQL lives in source.sql; successful non-secret tool requests can be recorded in source.evidenceFlow; transformations belong in query.methods. Metric definitions can be scoped to component IDs. Coverage and units are contractual metadata, not necessarily top-level keys. Source inspection displays saved evidence; it does not imply a rerun.

Under the Hood / implementation + sources
Architecture detail · interpretations identified in context

Preparation creates a new artifact identity and rejects an existing destination. Revisions preserve app/query/component IDs. DataComponent requires a non-empty stable ID. Identity gives references continuity; it is not a content hash, authorization token, or proof that evidence is unchanged.

07 / A pattern worth borrowing

Edit the presentation.
Preserve the evidence.

Rows, sources, and methods live in one state domain. Titles, layout, hidden blocks, and chart options live in another.

Evidence state · teaching fixture
Stored evidence is unchanged by presentation edits.
Advisor engagement18.4%Illustrative reviewed metric
Card hidden from this view. Evidence still exists.
Narrative: “Engagement is 18.4%.”
Evidence changed to 17.1%, but the sentence still says 18.4%. Refresh must recheck narrative, not only numbers.
Filters can change which stored rows are visible. Hiding a block or filtering a view does not revoke access to the underlying snapshot.
Under the Hood / implementation + sources
Architecture detail · interpretations identified in context
Presentation state is validated and stored separately. Hosted writes are owner-authorized and revision-checked; local state is keyed per artifact. The contract prohibits presentation editing from overriding reviewed values and source metadata. The simulated stale-narrative warning here teaches the refresh obligation; it is not a claim that Data automatically detects all stale prose.

More predictable artifacts. More framework responsibility.
Under the Hood / implementation + sources
Architecture detail · interpretations identified in context
The ordinary build verifies prebuilt runtime/compiler bytes, then links supported authored modules and local assets. The supported module set includes @openai/data-app, React/React DOM, React Markdown, JSX runtimes, and Recharts. Unsupported package/URL imports, top-level await, and lazy dynamic-import semantics are rejected. Vite belongs to maintainer or explicit source builds. Integrity checks are not a malicious-code sandbox or independent publisher signature.

10 / A durable object, not a disposable reply
The end of one request
is the start of a lifecycle.
A saved artifact can be delivered, edited, exported, and refreshed without forgetting what it is.
↶ Refresh → revalidate → deliver again
Under the Hood / implementation + sources
Architecture detail · interpretations identified in context
Split builds bind HTML to a content-addressed snapshot sidecar. Offline export embeds the verified data without recompiling. Publication packages exact compiled UI with a Worker and hosted data/presentation services: D1 for presentation and revision metadata, R2 for immutable indexed payloads. The current flow deploys before asset upload/readback, which creates a staging trade-off. Refresh reads the current snapshot, presentation, and deployed source; reruns saved requests; rebuilds; preserves identity/access; then checks the result.


11 / Where capabilities come from
The plugin defines the job.
The host makes it executable.
Data can reuse different governed tools because it does not embed every database and API client.
Codex Data owns
Workflow + artifact
  • Routing and analytical skills
  • Evidence and artifact contracts
  • Shared runtime and authoring rules
  • Validation and delivery workflows
Capability
contract⇄
Host / environment owns
Execution + authority
  • Source tools and authentication
  • Identity and permission enforcement
  • Browser / computer capabilities
  • Scheduling and deployment infrastructure
Conceptual capability switches
Under the Hood / implementation + sources
Architecture detail · interpretations identified in context
The manifest declares skills and optional connector categories, not a plugin-owned analytics MCP server. Actual source execution, browser actions, scheduling, and Sites hosting cross host boundaries. Worker write authorization assumes a trustworthy authenticated identity header supplied by the host. The capability switches summarize available operations; they do not test a live host or change real permissions.


12 / Translate architecture into practice
What should we steal?
Borrow the boundaries that make analytical work durable, inspectable, and easier to change.
Start with a clear contract. Add machinery when the product needs it.
Under the Hood / implementation + sources
Architecture detail · interpretations identified in context
These are engineering takeaways drawn from the source-backed architecture, not measured claims that adopting them improves every system. Each pattern needs a product need and a validation strategy. The original review retains the detailed implementation findings and prioritized plugin-improvement work.


13 / Calibrate the investment
Learn the principle.
Question the machinery.
A sophisticated artifact system solves a sophisticated product problem. A smaller agent may need much less infrastructure.
Copy a design because your constraints demand it—not because the source system has it.
Under the Hood / implementation + sources
Architecture detail · interpretations identified in context
The review identifies overlapping context/source-discovery guidance, multiple build and storage paths, rich heterogeneous metadata, and menu-based inspection complexity. Their impact is an architectural interpretation, not a benchmark or usability-study result. The plugin’s exact implementation is one point in a design space; its scale of investment is not a prerequisite for every analytical agent.


14 / Four words, now with depth
Agent → Skills
→ Evidence → Artifact
The model is the same. Now each word carries an architecture.
→→→
  1. Skills encode analytical responsibilities.
  2. Evidence is preserved, not merely consumed.
  3. Artifacts have stable contracts and identities.
  4. Presentation is separated from analytical evidence.
  5. The host executes capabilities; Data organizes the workflow and artifact experience.
Check your mental model
Why does a title edit not change the reviewed rows? Why can an offline artifact render but fail to refresh? What does a skill own that a tool does not?
Answers: separate state domains; refresh needs host execution and original source access; a skill defines the analytical responsibility and decision rules.
